steps.note: Open the single-stage event creation screen required for an RFQ.
Configure the event as a single-stage RFQ.
Every successful create flow requires an event title.
Apply the first available RFQ pricing template before adding line items.
Add the specified product and quantity.
Complete the pricing sheet, including the requested delivery location and other required cells.
Set and commit the 15-minute bidding duration; the catalog has no argument for the separate evaluation duration.
Invite exactly two QA test vendors for Vendor A and Vendor B without inventing supplier names.
Publish the RFQ so the vendors can submit quotes.
Confirm the event reached a real published project page.
Submit Vendor A's quote at 100 using the vendor portal.
Confirm Vendor A's quote was accepted.
Submit Vendor B's quote at 90 using the next distinct vendor portal identity.
Confirm Vendor B's quote was accepted.
Wait for the 15-minute bidding window to end naturally so the event can enter evaluation.
Observe that the event page shows evaluation status after bidding ends.
